residual_risks: Workpattern::Holidays.apply mutates the workpattern once per holiday date inside a loop (lib/workpattern/holidays.rb, self.apply: `::Holidays.between(...).map do |holiday| ... workpattern.resting(...) end`) with no rollback or transactional boundary. If an exception occurred partway through the loop (e.g. a future change to Workpattern#resting that adds validation, or a malformed date from the holidays gem), the caller would receive a raised exception but the workpattern would already have some holidays applied and others not, with no way to tell from the exception which dates succeeded. No evidence in the current code path that Workpattern#resting can raise for a valid in-range single date, so this is architectural/speculative rather than a confirmed defect -- not raised as a finding.

Workpattern::Holidays.apply performs an unsynchronized bulk mutation of a Workpattern instance (multiple workpattern.resting calls touching @weeks). The prior release (2d588b5) added a Mutex to the class-level named-workpattern *registry* (Workpattern.new/.get/.delete/.clear/.to_a/.from_h) but instance-level state mutation (the @weeks array touched by #resting/#working) was not brought under that lock and remains unsynchronized. This diff doesn't introduce concurrent usage itself, so it's pre-existing behavior being exercised through a new bulk-mutation entry point rather than a new bug -- flagged as a residual risk, not a finding, since it requires an external concurrent-caller scenario not evidenced in this diff.

The deliberate design of letting `require 'holidays'` raise Ruby's standard LoadError and letting `Holidays.between` raise Holidays::InvalidRegion propagate completely unwrapped (documented explicitly in the class comment and method doc in lib/workpattern/holidays.rb) is sound practice for a library adapter: it preserves the caller's ability to rescue the specific, well-known exception types rather than a library-invented wrapper, and avoids masking a genuine caller error (bad region) or environment error (missing gem) as a false success. No error-swallowing or misleading-default pattern was found anywhere in this file -- there is no rescue/catch block in lib/workpattern/holidays.rb at all, so nothing is being silently absorbed by the adapter itself.
testing_gaps: No test exercises Workpattern::Holidays.apply being called concurrently (from multiple threads) against the same Workpattern instance or against the shared holidays gem module state, which would be the natural next-step test given the immediately preceding release's focus on thread-safety of Workpattern's registry.

No test exercises what happens if Workpattern#resting itself raises partway through the Holidays.between(...).map loop (e.g. by stubbing #resting to raise on the second call) to confirm/document the partial-application behavior for callers who might rely on partial success or need to detect it.
